neighbours.label: ' to' naming the person or group a quality holds for, right after a predicate of knowing, interest, clarity, value or harm (known/unknown to, of interest to, familiar to, clear/obvious to, useful/acceptable to, dangerous/harmful to, matters to); quiet on infinitive 'to' (hard to solve, tried to), motion and giving 'to' (walked to, gave it to), fixed 'to' after similar/close/due/according/grateful/addressed/belongs, and 'to me' right after seem/look
neighbours.short: 'to' naming who a quality holds for (known to, of interest to)
fire: The author's real name was unknown to most of his readers.
These old trails are familiar to every hiker in the valley.
The answer seemed obvious to the students but not to the teacher.
Such chemicals are extremely harmful to fish and birds.
This report should be of interest to anyone who manages a small farm.
The new schedule was not acceptable to the union.
Her research proved enormously useful to later historians.
What matters to voters this year is the price of groceries.
quiet: The author's real name was hard to find in any of the records.
These old trails lead to a lake at the top of the valley.
The answer seemed obvious to me at first glance.
Such chemicals are similar to the ones used in cleaning products.
This report was addressed to the manager of a small farm.
The new schedule was changed due to the union strike.
Her research belongs to the university archive now.
Voters tried to understand the rising price of groceries.

predictions: Most fire items hold; the risky near miss is 'seemed obvious to me', which the label meant as bare 'seemed to me' and which will likely fire.
